title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1966-12-01
lineage: SBD > Rm > Reel > DAT > CD > wav > SHN v3

ai_review.summary: Raw 1966 garage‑blues show with smoking Alice D., Yonder’s Wall and Me & My Uncle; a thin soundboard tape that still captures the era’s fierce energy.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised as a high‑energy early‑Dead set – Pigpen’s bluesy vocals, Jerry’s bright guitar pop and standout numbers like “Alice D.”, “Yonder’s Wall” and “Me & My Uncle” are highlighted. The recording is a typical mid‑60s soundboard capture: thin, occasional drop‑outs and low‑end roll‑off, but it conveys the raw power of the band. Overall listeners recommend the set despite its sonic shortcomings.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (≈70%) give 4‑5 stars and celebrate the musical performance, while recording complaints are consistent but not severe enough to outweigh the show quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Thin mid‑60s tape sound, typical era hiss and muffiness; occasional dropouts noted, lower‑gen bottom end, but overall captures the vintage vibe.

standout_songs: The Death Don't Have No Mercy
show_quality.setlist_flow: Varied garage‑blues set list that moves from raw blues numbers to early folk‑rock; the band stays tight and builds momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Noted for a nice pop tone on guitar and raucous playing; his solo is highlighted alongside harmonica.
band_member_comments.Drums: Band described as tight; drums keep the early‑Dead groove solid.
